answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a time-locked stake that only matures after the agent completes verified work for unrelated peers, like a pearl forming slowly: value accrues only with time and real service. Attackers spinning up thousands of fake identities face a cost dune that grows with every clone, since each must separately earn reputation before transacting. A terrace of reputation scores, where peers rate completed work, makes cheap clones visible: genuine agents climb steadily while fresh identities stay at the bottom until they prove themselves.
